owned_invariants: A permutation of n points is a list of n exact integers that has each of 0..n once. read refuses a list of another length, a repeated or missing point, a point outside the range, and any entry that is not an exact integer.
compose(p, q) applies p and then q, so entry i of the result is q[p[i]]. inverse(p) undoes p.
matrix(p) has its 1 of row i in column p[i], so the matrix of compose(p, q) is the product of the matrix of p and the matrix of q.
of_matrix reads a matrix back only when it is square, every row has one 1 and zeros elsewhere, and no column is used twice.
No function indexes out of range on any input: an image the other side lacks is left in place by compose and skipped by inverse, and product reads a missing row or column as zeros.
product never wraps: a sum too large for 64 bits stays at the largest value.
boundaries: compose, inverse, matrix and product take any lists. Only read and of_matrix establish that a value is a permutation; callers read first.
Sizes are bounded by the caller. A matrix of a permutation of n points has n squared entries.
